newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Consob checks Olivetti price swing.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Consob checks Olivetti price swing.

text.p: Italian stock market regulator Consob has been calling stockbrokers in Milan to check who could be behind the heavy trading in information technology stock Olivetti, market sources said on Friday.
"Consob has been calling everybody to find out who is buying and who is selling the stock," said an equities trader with a Milan-based brokerage who asked not to be identified.
Other brokers also said they had received calls from the market regular. It is not unusual for Consob to conduct checks when there are unusual price movements in a company's stock.
Consob officials could not be reached for comment.
Olivetti's shares have been on a roller-coaster ride in recent weeks, plunging after former chairman Carlo De Benedetti resigned at the beginning of the month.
They sharply rebounded when Olivetti CEO Francesco Caio was ousted this week and replaced by Roberto Colaninno, a close ally of De Benedetti, but slid again on Friday.
Brokers in Milan believe that with more than 15 percent of the company's stock changing hands in less than three weeks, one or more buyers may be trying to build up a position in the company.

Italian newspapers have reported that De Benedetti, who is Olivetti's biggest single shareholder with just under 15 percent may also be buying shares in order to bolster his own position. --Milan newsroom +392-66102321
